sections.description: Adds a new disclosure that the current or future listing of Recorded Future as an "undesirable" or "unreliable" entity by certain jurisdictions could further increase information security risk, and escalates AI from threats that "may be further enhanced" by threat actors' use of AI to widespread AI use that "is enhancing" threat frequency and effectiveness and has "further exacerbated" fraud and cyber-attacks.

A.rationale: criterion 1 and 2: a new exposure tied to a named business (Recorded Future) and adverse jurisdictional listings is disclosed; criterion 3: the AI threat moves from hypothetical to realized; the cross-reference rename to "Privacy, Data, AI and Information Security" and page-header changes are minor on their own.

B.rationale: criterion 1 and 2: a new exposure tied to the named Recorded Future business and jurisdictional designations is disclosed, and criterion 3 applies to the could-to-is shift on AI threats; the cross-reference rename is minor but does not offset these.

sections.description: Adds network degradation, updates and migrations to new technology and platforms, and cybersecurity-related disruptions or failures at third-party service providers to the listed causes of service interruptions.

A.rationale: criterion 1: new sources of operational disruption risk are disclosed; the "disaster" to "disasters" change is stylistic.

B.rationale: criterion 1: new operational risk sources are disclosed, widening the scope of the disruption risk (criterion 3).

sections.description: The description of domestic switching changes from "with the exception of the U.S. and a select number of other jurisdictions, most in-country transactions" being switched by customers or other processors to Mastercard itself switching "a high percentage of domestic (or in-country) transactions", with customers switching only in "several jurisdictions".
